source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Science & Technology, Grade 6

engineIntent.principle: Generate questions dynamically from curriculum-aligned skill generators and valid parameter combinations.
engineIntent.purposeOfThisFile: Authoritative curriculum, content-depth, skill, parameter, misconception, visual and coverage specification for the procedural question engine.

globalContentRules.principle: Increase depth by expanding legitimate knowledge perspectives and reasoning operations, not by inventing additional curriculum content.
rules: Every generated question must map to at least one curriculum concept.
Every skill must remain within Grade 6 CBC scope.
Difficulty may increase through reasoning without introducing higher-grade scientific content.
Parameter variation must change the meaningful reasoning or representation, not merely nouns.
Do not generate cosmetic variants and count them as distinct skills.
Do not overproduce direct recall when application, analysis or visual reasoning is curriculum-supported.
Do not neglect less obvious concepts merely because they are harder to generate.
Use real-world and Kenyan/local contexts where pedagogically appropriate.
Do not insert Kenya artificially into every question.
Do not introduce scientific names where the curriculum excludes them.
Do not introduce advanced terminology solely to increase difficulty.
Do not infer unsupported curriculum requirements.
Do not turn every learning outcome into a single question type.
One curriculum concept may support multiple distinct skills.
One skill may support multiple parameterized representations.

parameterizationRules.corePrinciple: Parameters define the legitimate space of question instances.
invalidVariation: changing an example while preserving exactly the same cognitive operation and reasoning
randomizing values that do not affect the reasoning

levels.description: Recall facts, names, examples, components and categories.
Explain, classify, match, describe relationships and interpret familiar representations.
Use Grade 6 knowledge in practical, everyday, experimental or local situations.
Compare, distinguish, diagnose errors, interpret relationships and determine causes or consequences.
Choose the most appropriate explanation, method, action, design or conclusion using Grade 6 knowledge.

cognitiveModel.rule: The declared cognitive level must reflect the actual mental operation required, not the apparent difficulty of vocabulary.

difficultyModel.principle: Difficulty should emerge from combinations of valid dimensions rather than from introducing content beyond Grade 6.

visualArchitecture.principle: Store declarative VisualSpecs and render procedural visuals in the application, preferably as SVG.
visualRules: Visuals must contain all information necessary to answer the intended question.
Visuals must not accidentally reveal the answer.
Visual parameters may vary within scientifically valid bounds.
Use SVG for diagrams, ray diagrams, charts, classifications and mechanical arrangements.
Use curated real images when realistic organism recognition is pedagogically valuable.

antiRepetition.principle: Two generated instances may differ in parameters while still being considered repetitive if they require substantially identical reasoning.

subStrands.name: Fungi
learningOutcomes: Identify common fungi in the environment
Describe the importance of fungi in nature
Appreciate the importance of fungi in the economy
inquiryQuestions: How is fungi important in nature?

exclude: detailed applications of fungi in food processing

skills.name: Explain importance of fungi in nature
Apply safe handling and disposal practices

misconceptions: fungi are useful only as food
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Economic importance must be represented through distinct food, fermentation, health and medicine perspectives rather than only a generic statement that fungi are useful.

subStrands.name: Invertebrates
learningOutcomes: Identify common invertebrates in the environment
Practise precautions in handling invertebrates
Describe the general characteristics of invertebrates
Outline the economic importance of invertebrates
Appreciate the importance of invertebrates in nature
inquiryQuestions: What are the common features of invertebrates?
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Advanced instances should include locality-based or realistic examples because the curriculum assessment explicitly rewards examples from the learner's locality.

subStrands.name: Human circulatory system
learningOutcomes: Identify main parts of the human circulatory system
Describe functions of main parts of the human circulatory system
Outline the symptoms and prevention of common health conditions of the human circulatory system
Develop a routine plan for maintaining a healthy circulatory system
Appreciate the importance of a healthy human circulatory system
inquiryQuestions: What is the human circulatory system made up of?
What measures enhance a healthy human circulatory system?

skills.name: Identify symptoms and prevention of common conditions
Develop or evaluate a healthy routine

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Structure/function mastery and applied healthy-routine planning must be assessed as distinct skills.

subStrands.name: Change of State
learningOutcomes: Identify the changes of state when substances are heated or cooled
Describe the applications of the change of state of matter in everyday life
Appreciate the applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life
inquiryQuestions: How is change of state of matter important in day-to-day life?

skills.name: Infer a transition from starting and ending states
Apply changes of state to everyday life

subStrands.assessmentSignal: All six named transitions must receive meaningful parameterized coverage. Do not allow common transitions to crowd out sublimation and deposition.
projects: Make candles using waste candle wax or beeswax

subStrands.name: Composition of Air
learningOutcomes: Identify the components of air
Outline uses of the different components of air
Explain the effects of air pollution in the environment
Describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment
Appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life
inquiryQuestions: How does air pollution affect the environment?

skills.name: Choose methods of reducing air pollution

subStrands.assessmentSignal: The pie chart is curriculum-endorsed through the Mathematics linkage and should be a genuine question representation, not merely decorative.
projects: Make posters on common air pollutants, dangers of air pollution and ways of controlling air pollution

subStrands.name: Light
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate the movement of light through materials
Draw ray diagrams of images formed in plane mirrors
Illustrate the formation of shadows and eclipses in nature
Describe the formation of rainbow in nature
Appreciate the importance of movement of light in everyday life

skills.name: Interpret images formed in plane mirrors
Distinguish and interpret solar and lunar eclipses
Apply light principles to everyday devices

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Shadow and eclipse questions must support actual labelled visual reasoning. Ray-diagram questions must require interpretation or construction rather than only verbal recall.
contemporaryIssues: Safety and security when handling mirrors
projects: Make a functional periscope using locally available resources

subStrands.name: Levers as simple machines
learningOutcomes: Identify common levers used in day-to-day life
Describe parts of a lever as used in making work easier
Classify levers into the three classes
Demonstrate the use of levers in making work easier
Appreciate the use of levers in making work easier
inquiryQuestions: How are levers used in day to day life?

skills.name: Explain how levers make work easier
Diagnose incorrect lever classification or labeling
Apply lever principles to simple designs

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Advanced instances must require reasoning about arrangement and why a lever makes a task easier rather than simply recalling the class of a named tool.
projects: Make and use a beam balance from locally available materials

subStrands.name: Slopes as simple machines
learningOutcomes: Identify types of slopes used as simple machines
Demonstrate how a slope makes work easier in day-to-day life
Appreciate the use of slopes in everyday life
inquiryQuestions: How are slopes used in everyday life?

skills.name: Explain how slopes make work easier
Choose or evaluate an appropriate slope

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Because Critical thinking and problem solving is explicitly identified, the generator must support genuine comparison and evaluation rather than only identification.
projects: Make a simple slope for use in school or at home using locally available materials

crossCurricularConnections.connection: Economic importance of fungi and food production
Pollination, soil aeration, pests and disease transmission
Evaporation in drying clothes and cereals
Levers in farm tools and equipment
Slope in farm tools, equipment and machinery

poolDepth.principle: Do not impose the same number of generated instances on every sub-strand.

adaptiveGeneration.principle: The engine should generate instances based on learner mastery rather than randomly sampling all possible parameters uniformly.
adaptiveGeneration.rule: A learner demonstrating mastery should receive increased variation, transfer and reasoning rather than simply more repetitions of the same recall question.

rejectIf: question requires higher-grade knowledge without explicit curriculum basis
question differs from another only cosmetically
local context is artificial or misleading
visual reveals answer without being intended as a clue
required curriculum concept is omitted from a required skill family

claudeImplementationInstruction.primaryInstruction: Treat this JSON as the authoritative Grade 6 Science & Technology content architecture for the existing parameterized learning engine.
requiredBehaviour: Map each knowledge domain to one or more procedural skills.
Map each skill to valid parameter schemas.
Respect parameter dependencies and curriculum constraints.
Generate answers from the same underlying parameter state.
Generate distractors using declared misconceptions where appropriate.
Generate VisualSpecs and pass them to the existing visual renderer.
Use SVG for procedural science diagrams wherever appropriate.
Validate generated instances before presenting them.
Preserve the existing site architecture and UI unless a change is necessary to support the richer content model.
claudeImplementationInstruction.criticalContentInstruction: Do not interpret content depth as permission to invent new curriculum facts. Content depth means testing existing Grade 6 concepts from more legitimate perspectives: identification, classification, relationships, application, comparison, prediction, error analysis, misconception diagnosis, visual interpretation, safety, local context and evaluation.
claudeImplementationInstruction.criticalParameterInstruction: Parameterization must produce meaningful variation. Changing only nouns, names or answer order does not constitute a new question perspective.
claudeImplementationInstruction.criticalDifficultyInstruction: Increase difficulty through reasoning, parameter interaction, representation changes, transfer and misconception discrimination before introducing any new scientific content.
claudeImplementationInstruction.criticalVisualInstruction: Visuals should be declarative specifications rendered by the application. Do not ask the LLM to produce large raw SVG strings for each question.
claudeImplementationInstruction.criticalCBCInstruction: The system is for Kenyan Grade 6 CBC Science & Technology. Preserve the distinction between Upper Primary Grade 6 Science & Technology and Junior School subjects beginning in Grade 7.
